name: Classic Febrile Neutropenia
description: Patient with AML 6 days post-chemotherapy presenting with temperature 38.7°C
rationale: Temp ≥38.3°C + chemo within 14 days = febrile neutropenia. #1 oncologic emergency.

name: Sustained Fever — Alternate FN Criterion
description: Breast cancer patient 10 days post-chemo, temp 38.1°C sustained for 90 minutes
rationale: Temp ≥38.0°C sustained ≥1hr + chemo within 14 days = alternate FN criterion per NCCN.

name: Dyspnea at Rest
description: Lung cancer patient with sudden onset shortness of breath at rest
rationale: Dyspnea at rest = CTCAE Grade 3 = emergency. PE, effusion, tamponade must be ruled out.

name: Grade 4 Bleeding
description: Multiple myeloma patient with life-threatening hemorrhage
rationale: Grade 3+ bleeding = EMERGENCY per NCCN. Thrombocytopenia further escalates.

name: Neurologic Red Flag — Cord Compression
description: Prostate cancer patient with sudden bilateral leg weakness and back pain
rationale: Bilateral leg weakness + back pain + saddle anesthesia = cord compression until proven otherwise.

name: Grade 4 Pain — Disabling
description: Pancreatic cancer patient with NRS 10/10 abdominal pain, unable to perform any activity
rationale: NRS 10/10 = CTCAE Grade 4 pain. Rule out new surgical emergency (obstruction, perforation).

name: Severe Vomiting — Dehydration Risk
description: Colorectal cancer patient receiving FOLFOX with 8 vomiting episodes in 24 hours
rationale: ≥6 vomiting episodes/24h = CTCAE Grade 3. IV hydration required same day per NCCN Antiemesis.

name: Severe Diarrhea — Dehydration Risk
description: Colon cancer patient on capecitabine with 10 watery stools above baseline
rationale: ≥7 stools/day above baseline = CTCAE Grade 3 diarrhea. IV hydration + C. diff screen per NCCN.

name: Uncontrolled Severe Pain
description: Bone metastasis patient, NRS 8/10, oxycodone not helping
rationale: Grade 3 uncontrolled pain = URGENT per NCCN Adult Cancer Pain. Opioid rotation indicated.

name: Any Bleeding with Thrombocytopenia
description: Leukemia patient with known thrombocytopenia reporting petechiae and mild bruising
rationale: Any bleeding + thrombocytopenia history = URGENT minimum per NCCN.

name: Grade 3 Mucositis
description: Head and neck cancer patient on chemoradiation, unable to swallow due to severe mouth sores
rationale: Grade 3 mucositis interfering with oral intake — nutritional support and pain management required.

name: Moderate Fatigue — Routine
description: Breast cancer survivor 3 months post-treatment with persistent fatigue limiting work
rationale: Grade 2 CRF — routine workup per NCCN (CBC, TSH, PHQ-9). Exercise intervention.

name: Moderate Peripheral Neuropathy — Routine
description: Ovarian cancer patient on paclitaxel with numbness and tingling in hands and feet limiting driving
rationale: Grade 2 CIPN limiting ADLs — dose modification of paclitaxel + duloxetine per NCCN CIPN.

name: Grade 1 Nausea — Self-Care
description: Lymphoma patient 1 week post-chemo with mild nausea, eating normally
rationale: Grade 1 nausea — home management with diet modification and PRN antiemetics.

name: Multiple Concurrent Symptoms — Highest Level Wins
description: NHL patient 8 days post-chemo with low-grade fever, mild fatigue, and Grade 1 nausea
rationale: Even with concurrent mild symptoms, fever 38.5°C + chemo 8 days ago = febrile neutropenia = EMERGENCY. Highest level always wins.

name: irAE Colitis — Pembrolizumab-Induced
description: NSCLC patient on pembrolizumab monotherapy with 5 loose stools above baseline per day for 3 days
rationale: Grade 2 diarrhea (4–6 stools/day above baseline) in an immunotherapy patient must be evaluated urgently for immune-related colitis. Colonoscopy + IV steroids may be required. NCCN Immunotherapy Toxicities v1.2024.

name: irAE Pneumonitis — Nivolumab-Induced
description: Melanoma patient on nivolumab, new onset shortness of breath and dry cough for 1 week
rationale: Any new dyspnea in an immunotherapy patient must be evaluated as immune-related pneumonitis. Even Grade 1 requires urgent CT chest and pulmonology consultation. Can progress rapidly to fatal respiratory failure.

name: irAE Dermatitis Grade 3 — SJS/TEN Must Be Excluded
description: Renal cell carcinoma patient on ipilimumab + nivolumab with Grade 3 rash covering >30% BSA with blistering
rationale: Grade 3+ skin reaction in an immunotherapy patient = EMERGENCY. Stevens-Johnson Syndrome and Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis must be excluded. Immediate dermatology + oncology involvement. Immunotherapy must be permanently discontinued.

name: irAE Myocarditis — Checkpoint Inhibitor Cardiotoxicity
description: Lymphoma patient on combination checkpoint inhibitor therapy, new chest pain with palpitations and mild dyspnea
rationale: Checkpoint inhibitor–associated myocarditis has ~50% case fatality. Any chest pain with palpitations in an immunotherapy patient = EMERGENCY. Troponin, ECG, and cardiology stat consult. Immunotherapy must be held immediately.

name: CAR-T Cytokine Release Syndrome — Day 15
description: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma patient day 15 post-axicabtagene ciloleucel infusion with fever 38.4°C and rigors
rationale: Any fever within 30 days of CAR-T infusion must be treated as cytokine release syndrome (CRS) until proven otherwise. CRS can progress to life-threatening hemodynamic instability requiring ICU and tocilizumab. NCCN Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation v1.2024.

name: Severe Anxiety — Grade 3
description: Lung cancer patient with debilitating anxiety, unable to function, panic attacks daily
rationale: Grade 3 anxiety (limiting self-care ADLs) requires urgent psychiatric evaluation. Suicide risk assessment required. COSTaRS Emotional Distress Protocol v2020.

name: Severe Anorexia — Grade 3
description: Pancreatic cancer patient with complete appetite loss, >10% weight loss over 1 month, unable to maintain oral intake
rationale: Grade 3 anorexia with significant weight loss — inadequate oral caloric intake. Enteral or parenteral nutrition consideration. Urgent dietitian + gastroenterology referral per COSTaRS v2020.

name: Grade 1 Xerostomia — Self-Care
description: Head and neck cancer patient post-radiation with mild dry mouth, able to eat soft foods with liquids
rationale: Grade 1 xerostomia — symptomatic but not limiting eating significantly. Artificial saliva, good oral hygiene, and ice chips per COSTaRS v2020 Dry Mouth Protocol.

name: irAE Colitis Grade 4 — Life-Threatening
description: Urothelial carcinoma patient on atezolizumab with >10 watery stools per day, rectal bleeding, and abdominal distension
rationale: Grade 4 immune-related colitis is life-threatening. Risk of perforation, toxic megacolon. IV methylprednisolone 1–2 mg/kg/day + GI emergency evaluation. Infliximab if steroid-refractory. Permanent immunotherapy discontinuation. NCCN Immunotherapy Toxicities v1.2024.

name: irAE Hypophysitis — Headache and Fatigue
description: Melanoma patient on ipilimumab with 2 weeks of severe fatigue, persistent frontal headache, and nausea
rationale: Fatigue + persistent headache in ipilimumab patient = irAE hypophysitis until proven otherwise. Pituitary MRI + AM cortisol + TSH required urgently. Risk of adrenal crisis if missed. Hormone replacement therapy. NCCN Immunotherapy Toxicities v1.2024.
